title: Fourier degree of a decision tree is at most its depth
statement: Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be the $\pm 1$-valued function it computes, so that $f(x)=\sigma(T(x))$ where $\sigma$ sends $\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and $\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$. Then $f$ has Fourier degree at most the depth of $T$: for every $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $\hat f(S)\ne 0$, one has $\abs{S}\le\operatorname{depth}(T)$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n Boolean variables
f is the sign-encoded function computed by T
conclusion: every nonzero Fourier coefficient hat f(S) is supported on a set S with |S| at most depth(T)
replaced:
The function computed by a decision tree of depth $k$ has Fourier degree at most $k$:
$T.\mathrm{signEval}$ has degree at most $T.\mathrm{depth}$.
